title: Film Projectionist
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Chu Heng（Film projectionist Chu Heng around fifty, square glasses, worn deep-blue coveralls, film splicer in the breast pocket, fingers blackened by carbon dust） pushes open the Booth Two（Theater Booth Two, twin projectors side by side, sound-damping felt on the walls, air smelling of ozone and film） door and lights the carbon-arc lamphouse（A cast-iron carbon-arc lamphouse, observation window intact, carbon-rod gap precise, painted dark green） for a test.
A row of five booth wall lamps（A row of five booth wall lamps mounted above the sound-damping felt, shades polished bright） above the sound-damping felt; Chu Heng wipes each shade clean.

Two changeover bells（Two changeover copper bells hung by the projection port, clappers scarred, ringing twice lightly at changeover） hang by the projection port; Chu Heng taps them lightly—clear bright rings.
Chu Heng checks the carbon-arc lamphouse rod gap and observation window, confirming no cracks.
Through the projection port Chu Heng watches the light patch on the empty screen.
The intact carbon-arc lamphouse sits steady on its base; the observation window reflects warm wall-lamp light.
Chu Heng sits on a folding chair and drinks cold tea.
Far audience entry sounds rise; he puts his glasses back on.
He trims a sprocket fringe with the splicer.
Chu Heng opens the black-cover show logbook（A black-cover show logbook recording reel numbers and run times, neat handwriting） and notes today's reel numbers.
He sketches a changeover timeline on the page.
Chu Heng closes the show logbook and tucks it into the worktable drawer.
White light from the carbon-arc lamphouse sweeps his cheek.
He tears a corner of lens tissue and wipes carbon dust from his glasses.

On the morning film-vault platform（Back-alley film-vault platform, yellow unload lines on the concrete, iron door half open, empty film cases stacked）, Chu Heng greets the arriving vermilion film trailer（A vermilion film trailer with metal film cases fixed in the bed, white 'Print' lettering on the body）.

Young Yunduo（Young Yunduo: a lean projection apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, hair clip holding a light-blue film sprocket scrap, oversized deep-blue coveralls, bright stubborn eyes） jumps down from the film trailer; the light-blue sprocket scrap on the hair clip sways lightly.

Chu Heng points to the first-run three reel labels（Three cardboard reel labels stuck on the first-run film case, lettered 'Reel 1', 'Reel 2', 'Reel 3'） and teaches Yunduo to tell Reel 1 through Reel 3.
Yunduo squats by the platform yellow line and curiously touches the copper corners of empty film cases.
Chu Heng explains to Yunduo that two rings of the changeover bells mean switch machines.
Yunduo looks back at the intact film trailer, eyes full of longing.
The iron door creaks lightly; they walk toward Booth Two.

In the print-vault narrow corridor（A narrow corridor between print vaults, tall iron racks on both sides, fire-sand on the floor, heavy shadow）, A-Yu（Young projection worker A-Yu whose face closely resembles Yunduo's, but an orange-red dust mask hung at the neck, ash-gray vest over coveralls, swaggering look） with an orange-red dust mask at the neck turns from iron-rack shadow.
A-Yu walks slowly on the fire-sand; the ash-gray vest stands out.
He brushes past a mate carrying film cases; the mask flashes in the reflection.
A-Yu knocks the iron rack to confirm the case pins are locked.
He passes the corridor end toward the inspection table.
On the film-vault platform Yunduo and A-Yu stand side by side: one clipping a light-blue sprocket scrap, one with an orange-red dust mask at the neck.
Yunduo hands a test scrap to A-Yu; they lock eyes briefly.
A-Yu tidies Yunduo's oversized coverall collar, then turns away.
They walk opposite ways along the yellow line; shadows cross in the iron-door gloom.
A rewind whir rises; only empty cases lightly knock on the platform.
Months later at night, Chu Heng keeps watch alone in Booth Two.
He opens the show logbook（The same show logbook soaked through with carbon dust, cover gray, writing blurred into a paste）; the cover is soaked through with carbon dust, gray and blurred.
Chu Heng wipes the carbon-arc lamphouse observation window with lens tissue.
From the projection port he watches one emergency light in the pitch-black auditorium.
The carbon-arc lamphouse sits still on its base; the rods glow faintly dull.
A changeover bell is bumped half a ring by vent draft, then falls silent.
At spring-slate open, Chu Heng day after day focuses and tests in the booth.
Another rainy night he wraps his coveralls tight and keeps watch by the carbon-arc lamphouse.
At high-summer noon the machine room stifles; he rotates opening windows to cool it.
Autumn fog thickens; wall-lamp light struggles through the dust.
On New Year's Eve Chu Heng alone fills the show logbook to the last page.
In early spring he recalibrates the gate and keeps testing prints.
Before rainy season Chu Heng reinforces the vault fire-sand layer.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small bucket of dry sand in the booth corner.
Before another Golden Rooster festival he checks sprockets reel by reel.
On a snowy night with no show Chu Heng leaves only one booth wall lamp and keeps vigil till dawn.
After Insects Awaken he wipes the dried splice table clean again.
Around Qingming he clears weeds at the old outdoor screen frame entrance.
At Grain Rain he teaches an apprentice to identify newly arrived color prints.
Chu Heng replaces carbon rods and adjusts the gap.
He checks the take-up gear and drips machine oil.
The intact carbon-arc lamphouse is lit again by him; the observation window shows white light.
Unload sounds rise from the platform; he looks up to listen.
Chu Heng dumps spent carbon slag into an iron bucket and lids it.
At noon break he drinks tea by the projection port; tea smoke curls past his glasses.
In the afternoon he tests again, focusing all four screen corners.
At sunset he kills the main switch and locks the booth.
Before night he patrols the print vault once more, confirming no smoke smell.
At dawn Chu Heng patrols the film-vault platform; the film trailer still sits inside the yellow line.
He crouches to check whether the film trailer bed case straps have loosened.
On the first run, those earlier three reel labels still stick in place.
A blue-gray handcart（A blue-gray cleaning handcart, wide flat body, no film-case mounting frame—not the same as the film trailer） rolls across the platform—wide flat body, no 'Print' lettering.
Chu Heng stands on the platform noting last night's damp cores.
He re-clips the film trailer hitch tight.
A sanitation truck passes far off; morning mist begins to thin.
At nightfall Chu Heng returns to Booth Two and opens the carbon-dust-stained show logbook.
Against old numbers he backfills today's changeover times.
He briefly lights the carbon-arc lamphouse; white light shows the logbook's dusty gray cover.
He wipes fresh carbon dust from his glasses.
Vent draft rises; the sound-damping felt rustles lightly.
Chu Heng kills half the booth wall lamps, leaving only the one at the machine.
In a storm the carbon arc overloads; Booth Two falls into scramble.
Sparks fly; wall lamps shake hard.

As Chu Heng fights the blaze the carbon-arc lamphouse（The same carbon-arc lamphouse: observation window shattered, carbon rods broken and blackened, scorched patches on the outer wall） observation window shatters; the rods break.
On the platform the film trailer is ignited by flying sparks and smokes hard.
Flames lick the film cases; the film trailer（The film trailer ignited by carbon-arc sparks, cases melted, frame charred and twisted） burns in the fire, frame charred black.
Chu Heng clutches the shattered carbon-arc lamphouse and will not let go.
Alarms blare; the corridor fills with footsteps.
Next day when rain eases, Chu Heng stands in the booth staring at the carbon-exploded carbon-arc lamphouse.
He strokes the shattered observation-window frame with a finger, expression darkened.
On a blank page of the show logbook he writes the date the film trailer burned.
The film trailer's unload flowchart is still taped to the wall; Chu Heng gazes a long time.
He takes down one of the five booth wall lamps above the sound-damping felt and sits alone by its faint light.
The shattered carbon-arc lamphouse rests on its base like an extinguished eye.
Far sweeping sounds rise; charred scraps are gathered into a heap.
Weeks later Chu Heng brings glass and carbon rods, ready to repair the carbon-arc lamphouse.

From the vault he rolls out a xenon spare housing（A xenon spare housing, vaguely like the carbon-arc lamphouse but shorter, silver-gray paint, no observation window）—somewhat like the lamphouse but shorter and silver-gray.
Chu Heng fits a new observation window and recalibrates the carbon-rod gap.

After grinding the scorched patches, the carbon-arc lamphouse（The carbon-arc lamphouse fitted with a new observation window, rod gap recalibrated, scorched patches ground down so it can ignite again） can ignite again.
He briefly tests the light; white beam steady and sharp again.
Chu Heng rolls the xenon spare housing back to the vault, no longer confusing them.

A silver-gray cargo electric cart（A brand-new silver-gray cargo electric cart loaded with cardboard boxes, no 'Print' lettering—utterly unlike the film trailer） rolls onto the film-vault platform—nothing like the burned film trailer.

A Theater firefighter（A lean theater firefighter in a red helmet and ochre fire jacket, build somewhat like Chu Heng's, but a fire crest on the arm patch） in red helmet and ochre jacket steps onto the platform and talks beside Chu Heng; the two builds are close.
The firefighter points at the silver-gray cargo electric cart and explains the temporary print haul.
The electric cart drives off; Chu Heng alone watches it leave the platform.
He resticks the reel labels straight and walks back to the booth.

Into the print-vault narrow corridor comes intern print checker Xiao Ni（New intern print checker Xiao Ni, light-purple headscarf, brand-new coveralls; at a glance like young Yunduo, but sharper chin and shy eyes） in a light-purple headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Yunduo.
Xiao Ni tries winding film, but Chu Heng shakes his head—she is not Yunduo after all.
Xiao Ni bows her head and withdraws; only iron-rack shadow remains in the corridor.

Years later at dusk, Chu Heng（The same Chu Heng: scorched cuffs, glasses filmed with ash, walking slowly supporting himself on the projection port, eyes heavy） with scorched cuffs and ash-filmed glasses stands under the old outdoor screen frame（An old outdoor screen frame in the suburbs, white cloth tattered, supports rusted, weeds over the base） as if supporting a projection port.
He looks up at the tattered white cloth, gaze distant.
Far off those two changeover bells by a projection port ring lightly in the wind; Chu Heng stops to listen.
He presses his palm to the rusted support, as if saying goodbye.
Weeds sway; the screen frame grows quieter.

By day, adult Yunduo（Adult Yunduo: a broader-shouldered projectionist in his twenties, still clipping the light-blue sprocket scrap, coveralls fitted, steady eyes） returns along the back alley and hurries toward the old outdoor screen frame.
Under the screen frame Yunduo reunites with smoke-weary Chu Heng; they support each other.
Beside the booth folding cot, Yunduo holds Chu Heng's withered hand.
Chu Heng（Chu Heng has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the booth folding cot, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies.
Outside, rewind sound stills; alley wind falls quiet for an instant.
Behind the booth door Chu Heng's deep-blue coveralls still hang; Yunduo reaches to stroke them lightly.

By the doorframe, adult Yunduo stands before the newly nailed projection memorial brass plaque（A brass memorial plaque nailed to the booth doorframe, engraved 'Chu Heng' and the hire year, verdigris on the edges）.
Yunduo's fingertip traces Chu Heng's name engraved on the plaque.
He softly speaks the page number of the logbook noting the film trailer burn, as if answering.
After ash is cleared on the film-vault platform, Yunduo writes the words film trailer in the empty bay then erases them.
Passing the booth corridor he sees Chu Heng's old splicer in a glass case.
In the night Yunduo softly repeats Chu Heng's changeover cues to the empty machine base.
In the film smell Yunduo grips the light-blue sprocket scrap tight in his palm.

A-Yu（A-Yu after a makeover still wears the orange-red dust mask at the neck; vest swapped for matte black, expression deeper） after a makeover arrives from the print vault and briefly locks eyes with Yunduo under the old outdoor screen frame.
Yunduo and A-Yu stand side by side by the rusted support—one calm-eyed, one deep-faced.
A-Yu still wears the orange-red dust mask at the neck; Yunduo still clips the light-blue sprocket scrap.
They are silent a moment, then each turns and leaves the screen frame.
The shot returns to years ago—the youth who jumped from the vermilion trailer with a light-blue sprocket scrap clipped in the hair appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the booth, a dark-green cast-iron lamphouse ignites white light for the first time.
Flash to the print corridor—the figure with orange-red mask at the neck and ash-gray vest flickers past.
Again that row of five old shaded wall lamps above the sound-damping felt appears.
Back to the concrete platform by the unload yellow line of first meeting; the iron door as before.
Yunduo reopens that carbon-dust-stained show logbook and walks into Booth Two.
On the first-run film case, those earlier three reel labels still stick.
Yunduo lights the window-retuned carbon-arc lamphouse; white light fills the screen again.
He rolls his coverall cuffs tight and nods confirmation the way Chu Heng once did.
In theater dusk the new shift's changeover bells ring twice lightly.
Before the projection port Yunduo drops today's first beam.
Far in the auditorium a seat flips up faintly.
